nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a finite set of attributes, $F$ a finite set of functional dependencies over $A$ and $X \subseteq A$. The attribute closure $X^+$ of $X$ under $F$ is computed by the closure algorithm: starting from $X$, repeat closure rounds (each adds the right side of every dependency of $F$ whose left side is already included) until nothing changes, for at most $|A|$ rounds.
nodes.title: Attribute closure

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies, $n$ a natural number and $Y$ a finite set of attributes. The loop returns $Y$ if $n = 0$ or if one closure round for $F$ leaves $Y$ unchanged; otherwise it returns the loop with $n - 1$ rounds started from the result of one closure round applied to $Y$. Thus it repeats closure rounds from $Y$ until nothing changes, for at most $n$ rounds.
nodes.title: Iterated closure rounds

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a finite set of attributes, $F$ a finite set of functional dependencies over $A$ and $X \subseteq A$. Applying one closure round for $F$ to the attribute closure $X^+$ of $X$ under $F$ returns $X^+$.
nodes.title: The attribute closure is a fixed point of a closure round

nodes.summary: For a finite set $F$ of functional dependencies and a finite set $Y$ of attributes, one closure round returns $Y$ together with the right side of every dependency of $F$ whose left side is contained in $Y$, that is, the set $Y \cup \bigcup \{R : (L \to R) \in F,\ L \subseteq Y\}$.
nodes.title: One round of the attribute-closure algorithm

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a finite set of attributes, $F$ a finite set of functional dependencies over $A$ and $X \subseteq A$. The closure witness relation for $X$ is the relation with values in $\{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ whose tuples are the tuple that is $\mathrm{true}$ on every attribute and the tuple that is $\mathrm{true}$ exactly on the attribute closure $X^+$ of $X$ under $F$. These two tuples agree exactly on…
nodes.title: Closure witness relation

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies and $X$, $Y$, $Z$ finite sets of attributes with $Z \subseteq Y$. If $X \to Y$ is derivable from $F$ with Armstrong's axioms, then so is $X \to Z$.
nodes.title: Decomposition rule

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a finite set of attributes, $F$ a finite set of functional dependencies over $A$ and $f$ a functional dependency over $A$. Then $f$ is derivable from $F$ with Armstrong's axioms if and only if $F$ entails $f$, that is, $f$ holds in every relation (with values in any type) that satisfies every dependency of $F$. In other words, Armstrong's axioms are sound and complete for functional dependencies.
nodes.title: Armstrong's theorem

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a finite set of attributes, $F$ a finite set of functional dependencies over $A$ and $X, Y \subseteq A$. Then $X \to Y$ is derivable from $F$ with Armstrong's axioms if and only if $Y \subseteq X^+$, where $X^+$ is the attribute closure of $X$ under $F$ computed by the closure algorithm.
nodes.title: The closure algorithm decides derivability

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a finite set of attributes, $F$ a finite set of functional dependencies over $A$ and $f$ a functional dependency over $A$. If $f$ holds in every relation with values in $\{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ that has at most two tuples and satisfies every dependency of $F$, then $f$ is derivable from $F$ with Armstrong's axioms.
nodes.title: Completeness of Armstrong's axioms, two-tuple form

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies over a set $A$ of attributes. Derivability from $F$ is the least property of functional dependencies over $A$ such that, for all finite sets $X$, $Y$, $Z$ of attributes: every dependency of $F$ is derivable; $X \to Y$ is derivable whenever $Y \subseteq X$ (reflexivity); if $X \to Y$ is derivable, then so is $X \cup Z \to Y \cup Z$ (augmentation); and if $X \to Y$…
nodes.title: Derivability with Armstrong's axioms

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a type of attributes. A finite set $F$ of functional dependencies on $A$ entails a functional dependency $f$ on $A$ when, for every type $V$ and every relation $r$ with values in $V$ (a set of tuples $A \to V$) that satisfies $F$, the dependency $f$ holds in $r$.
nodes.title: Entailment of functional dependencies

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies on a finite set of attributes $A$, and let $K$ be a superkey for $F$. Let $V$ be a type of values. If a relation $r$, a set of tuples $A \to V$, satisfies $F$, then any two tuples $t, u \in r$ that agree on every attribute of $K$ are equal.
nodes.title: Tuples that agree on a superkey are equal

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies on a finite set of attributes $A$. Every superkey $K$ for $F$ has a subset $K' \subseteq K$ that is a candidate key for $F$.
nodes.title: Every superkey contains a candidate key

nodes.summary: A functional dependency $X \to Y$ over a type $A$ of attributes consists of two finite sets of attributes $X, Y \subseteq A$: the determining attributes $X$ (its left side) and the determined attributes $Y$ (its right side).
nodes.title: Functional dependency

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies on a finite set of attributes $A$, and let $l$ be a list in which every attribute of $A$ occurs. Then the output of the key-finding algorithm on $F$ and $l$, which starts from the set of all attributes and goes through $l$ in order, removing each listed attribute whenever what remains is still a superkey, is a candidate key for $F$.
nodes.title: The key-finding algorithm returns a candidate key

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies on a finite set of attributes $A$, and let $l$ be a list of attributes. The key-finding algorithm starts from the set $K = A$ of all attributes and goes through $l$ in order: for each listed attribute $a$, it replaces $K$ by $K \setminus \{a\}$ when the attribute closure of $K \setminus \{a\}$ under $F$ is all of $A$, and keeps $K$ otherwise. It returns the final…
nodes.title: Key-finding algorithm

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies on a finite set of attributes $A$. For every set $X \subseteq A$ of attributes, the closure witness relation for $X$ under $F$ satisfies $F$.
nodes.title: The closure witness satisfies the dependencies

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a type of attributes and $V$ a type of values. A functional dependency $X \to Y$ on $A$ holds in a relation $r$, a set of tuples $A \to V$, when any two tuples $t, u \in r$ that agree on every attribute of $X$ also agree on every attribute of $Y$.
nodes.title: A functional dependency holds in a relation

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies on a finite set of attributes $A$. A set $K \subseteq A$ of attributes is a candidate key for $F$ if and only if $K$ is a superkey for $F$ and, for every $a \in K$, the set $K \setminus \{a\}$ is not a superkey for $F$.
nodes.title: Candidate keys are the superkeys minimal under single removals

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies on a finite set of attributes $A$. A set $K \subseteq A$ of attributes is a candidate key for $F$ when $K$ is a superkey for $F$ and no proper subset of $K$ is a superkey for $F$.
nodes.title: Candidate key

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies over a finite set of attributes $A$. A set of attributes $K$ is a superkey for $F$ when the dependency $K \to A$ is derivable from $F$ with Armstrong's axioms, that is, $K$ determines every attribute.
nodes.title: Superkey

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies over a finite set of attributes and $X$ a set of attributes. An attribute $a$ lies in the attribute closure $X^+$ of $X$ under $F$, as computed by the closure algorithm, if and only if the dependency $X \to \{a\}$ is derivable from $F$ with Armstrong's axioms.
nodes.title: The closure algorithm computes the attribute closure

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies over a finite set of attributes. If $K$ is a superkey for $F$ and $K \subseteq K'$, then $K'$ is a superkey for $F$.
nodes.title: Supersets of superkeys are superkeys

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies and $X, Y, W, Z$ finite sets of attributes. If $X \to Y$ and $Y \cup W \to Z$ are derivable from $F$ with Armstrong's axioms, then so is $X \cup W \to Z$.
nodes.title: Pseudotransitivity rule

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies over a finite set of attributes, $X$ a set of attributes and $X^+$ its attribute closure under $F$. For every dependency $Y \to Z$ in $F$ with $Y \subseteq X^+$, also $Z \subseteq X^+$.
nodes.title: The attribute closure is closed under the dependencies

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies over attributes $A$, and let $r$ be a relation, given as a set of tuples $A \to V$ with values in a type $V$. Then $r$ satisfies $F$ when every dependency of $F$ holds in $r$.
nodes.title: A relation satisfies a set of dependencies

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies over a finite set of attributes. Given a list $l$ of attributes and a set of attributes $K$, go through $l$ in order and, for each attribute $a$, remove $a$ from the current set whenever the attribute closure under $F$ of the current set without $a$ is the set of all attributes (that is, the set without $a$ is still a superkey); the result is the set reached at the…
nodes.title: Shrinking a key along a list

nodes.summary: A derivable dependency holds in every relation satisfying `F`.
nodes.title: Armstrong's axioms are sound

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies and $X, Y$ finite sets of attributes. If $X \to Y$ is derivable from $F$ with Armstrong's axioms, then so is $X \to X \cup Y$.
nodes.title: Adding the left side to the right side

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies and $X, Y, Z$ finite sets of attributes. If $X \to Y$ and $X \to Z$ are derivable from $F$ with Armstrong's axioms, then so is $X \to Y \cup Z$.
nodes.title: Union rule

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
